problem: Express $z=\frac{4}{1+2\text{i}}$ in the form $r(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).$ Give $\theta $ in radians to three decimal places.
worked_solution:
First, we express the given complex number in the form $z=x+y\text{i}.$ To do this, we remove $\text{i}$ from the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator of $z$ by the complex conjugate of the denominator, which is $1-2\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{4}{1+2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{4(1-2\text{i})}{(1+2\text{i})(1-2\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{4(1-2\text{i})}{{1}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4(1-2\text{i})}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}-\frac{8}{5}\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $r$ represents the magnitude $|z|.$ For a complex number $z=x+y\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.
$$

So, for $z=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{8}{5}\text{i},$ the magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}+{(-\frac{8}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{4}^{2}+{8}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{80}{25}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16\cdot 5}{25}} \\  & =\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar form, $\theta $  represents the argument $\operatorname{arg}⁡(z).$ Since $x=\frac{4}{5}$ is positive and $y=-\frac{8}{5}$ is negative, $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we can find $\theta $ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{(-\frac{8}{5})}{(\frac{4}{5})}| \\  & =2\pi -\operatorname{arctan}⁡2 \\  & ≈5.176,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. 

Finally, we write the complex number $z$ in polar form:

$$
z=\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(5.176)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5.176)).
$$
